subject: Engineering decisions
title: `wf metro start|restart` in Rust
question: What was measured for `wf metro start|restart` in Rust?
method: Transcribed from the cited historical record. Units and precision follow the source.
finding: Not exercised: a real `expo`, a held port that needs the SIGKILL escalation, the 180 s timeout path, and the vault load against a real backend. Wall time of a start is the 1 s readiness poll either way (about 1.4 s per test on both), so there is no startup saving worth a table here; what changes is that `wf` itself no longer needs Node for the start.

rows: Decision: port the start path: port reservation (reuse or allocate `max + 1`, default from `WF_METRO_PORT_MIN`), kill and wait for the port, the log-forwarding and backend environment (best-effort vault load of just the keys involved, through a new `load_keys_into_process_env`), `.expo/metro-port.json`, the supervised `sh` restart loop or a direct `npx expo start`, a detached spawn into `/tmp/metro-<port>.log`, the 1 s readiness poll of `/status`, and the TS's failure message with the log tail. `restart` is stop plus start with its own log lines. Two start variants still go to the TS, decided before anything is touched: a set `EXPO_PUBLIC_INITIAL_ROUTE` (route pre-warm) and a configured OTLP pair (the BetterStack log forwarder process). `ensure` with Metro down also still goes to the TS.

Not exercised: a real `expo`, a held port that needs the SIGKILL escalation, the 180 s timeout path, and the vault load against a real backend. Wall time of a start is the 1 s readiness poll either way (about 1.4 s per test on both), so there is no startup saving worth a table here; what changes is that `wf` itself no longer needs Node for the start.
